title: Effects of range of motion on muscle development during resistance training interventions: A systematic review
key_findings: Full range of motion appears better than partial range for lower-body hypertrophy.
Evidence for the upper limbs is limited and conflicting, and no study had looked at trunk muscles.
Some evidence suggests the response to range of motion may differ by muscle.
methods: Systematic review of longitudinal dynamic training studies, quality rated with a modified PEDro scale; no pooled meta-analysis.
limitations: Six studies, mostly men; upper-body conclusions not possible.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
